mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined monotonically for three consecutive weeks (3.7 to -13.3). This downward momentum reflects an ongoing contraction in discretionary mobility that will persist into the next four weeks absent a reversal signal.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days despite the three-week decline trend.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility crossed a steep decline threshold (-9.1 to -16.7 week-on-week), indicating reduced outdoor substitution activity in cold weather or rising case concern. This loss of an outdoor alternative does not offset indoor retail declines but instead co-moves with them, signaling further RETAIL_REC weakness over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 6 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -9.1 to -16.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week even though PARKS declined by more than 6 points, falsifying the co-movement assumption.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL (4.9 to 9.3) and decline in TRANSIT (3.3 to -8.7) jointly indicate an intensifying stay-at-home behavioral shift. When both series move in these directions together, people reduce out-of-home errands including retail trips, compounding the suppression of RETAIL_REC beyond what either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rising and TRANSIT falling concurrently for two or more weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose while TRANSIT fell across t-3w through t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is higher than prior 28 days despite continued joint RESIDENTIAL increase and TRANSIT decrease.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp co-decline of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside RETAIL_REC in the most recent week is consistent with newly imposed or tightening public-health restrictions (e.g., capacity limits, advisories) in a policy-tightening regime. Under this regime, restrictions suppress commuting and retail simultaneously, and the suppression persists until restrictions ease, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both negative at t-0w alongside RETAIL_REC decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed, indicating the mechanism does not hold under this regime.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained persistently elevated (48-54 percent above baseline) across all four weeks while RETAIL_REC fell, consistent with a seasonal post-holiday pattern where households substitute discretionary retail trips for essential grocery/pharmacy trips during January cold-and-illness season. This substitution pattern is expected to continue, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed for the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed above 48 while RETAIL_REC fell from 3.7 to -13.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers toward positive territory even as GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, indicating substitution logic does not explain the divergence.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen in each of the last four weeks (4.9 to 9.3), functioning as a leading indicator of overall reduced out-of-home activity. Because RESIDENTIAL increases typically precede broad declines in out-of-home categories by one to two weeks, this sustained rise predicts continued RETAIL_REC weakness over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise, breaking the assumed lead-lag relationship.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls below a -8 point threshold, as observed at t-0w (-8.7), reduced transit usage mechanically limits access to retail and recreation destinations that rely on public transit for footfall, producing an immediate one-week drag on RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -8.7 at t-0w, crossing the -8 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week immediately following a TRANSIT reading below -8, invalidating the threshold linkage.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has been highly volatile (-4.3, -14.9, 6.0, -0.6), suggesting unstable return-to-office patterns possibly tied to intermittent remote-work mandates during an active wave. When combined with falling RETAIL_REC, this volatility signals that workplace-linked lunch and after-work retail trips remain suppressed and erratic, limiting any near-term rebound in RETAIL_REC despite occasional positive WORKPLACES weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week swings exceed 10 points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES swung from -14.9 to 6.0 to -0.6 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds steadily over the next two weeks even as WORKPLACES continues to exhibit large week-on-week swings, contradicting the volatility-suppression link.
